sections.title: Multisensory Design
sections.description:
This seminar explores design as a fully embodied, multisensory practice that extends beyond sight to engage sound, touch, smell, taste, movement, and spatial perception.
Students will investigate how sensory experiences shape meaning, emotion, accessibility, and behavior across contexts such as product design, spatial design, interaction design, art, and emerging technologies.
Through hands-on projects, readings from design theory, neuroscience, and sensory studies, and analysis of contemporary practitioners, students will learn to design experiences that are inclusive, immersive, and responsive to the body in space.
Emphasis is placed on sensory ethics, accessibility, and cultural variation, as well as experimentation with materials, technologies, and environments. By the end of the course, students will develop a critical and practical framework for creating multisensory design systems that communicate, provoke, and connect at a human scale.
